title: Warm-fleet routing and recovery lab
description: See how model locality, load balance, scaling delay, and fallback policy shape the user-visible incident.

incidents.label: Steady traffic
incidents.detail: A popular model receives predictable demand with no worker loss.

incidents.label: Long-tail catalog
incidents.detail: Many model versions compete for limited accelerator memory.

incidents.label: Zone loss
incidents.detail: Three warm replicas disappear while retries increase demand.

routingPolicies.label: Round robin
routingPolicies.detail: Spreads requests evenly without considering queue or model residency.

routingPolicies.label: Least loaded
routingPolicies.detail: Protects queue balance but may send requests to cold workers.

routingPolicies.label: Locality plus load
routingPolicies.detail: Prefers resident models until queue pressure makes another worker safer.

scalingSignals.label: GPU utilization
scalingSignals.detail: A lagging signal that rises after work reaches the accelerator.

scalingSignals.label: Active concurrency
scalingSignals.detail: Tracks admitted work but does not include every queued request.

scalingSignals.label: Queue age
scalingSignals.detail: A leading pressure signal when prediction deadlines are known.
